title: A high performance liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry protocol for detection of neurotransmitters in the rat brain tissue
author: Dai, Qin, et al.

steps.title: Prepare Rat PD Model
steps.instruction: Generate the rat Parkinson's disease (PD) model via unilateral injection of rotenone into the right substantia nigra pars compacta (SNpc).

substeps.instruction: Inject 12 μg of rotenone into the right SNpc.
Perfuse through the left ventricle with saline for approximately 8 min (until lavage fluid from the right auricle is clear).
Extract brains immediately and store at −80 °C.

steps.title: Prepare Rat AD Model
steps.instruction: Generate the female aged rat Alzheimer's disease (AD) model using soluble Aβ 1–42 oligomers.

substeps.instruction: Implant a fixed cannula in the right lateral ventricle (RV) at coordinates: L = 1.5 mm, AP = 1.0 mm, DV = 3.8 mm.
Administer 3.36 μg of soluble Aβ oligomers over 3 weeks.

steps.title: Homogenize Brain Tissue
steps.instruction: Dissect and homogenize the target brain regions using a tissue homogenizer.

substeps.instruction: Dissect striata from PD models and hippocampus from AD models.
Homogenize for 30 s using 5 μl of 0.1% FA per mg of brain tissue.

steps.title: Extract and Filter Supernatant
steps.instruction: Isolate the supernatant from the homogenate and filter for purity.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge samples at 14,000 rpm at 4 °C for 10 min.
Filter the supernatant through a 0.22 μm filter.

steps.title: Dilute Samples
steps.instruction: Dilute the filtered supernatant with 0.1% FA solution based on the target analyte and brain region.

substeps.instruction: For PD striata: dilute 20 times for ACH and DA; dilute 250 times for GABA, GLU, and GLN.
For AD hippocampus: dilute 30 times for ACH and DA; dilute 600 times for GABA, GLU, and GLN.

steps.title: Perform HPLC-MS/MS Analysis
steps.instruction: Inject the diluted samples into the HPLC-MS/MS system.

substeps.instruction: Use an Agilent 1290 HPLC system coupled with an Agilent-6430 mass spectrometer.
Inject 20 μl of the sample using an autosampler.

description: All standards and samples displayed good response values and representative chromatographic peaks are shown in Fig. 1. Because all of the analytes targets are endogenous metabolites, the determination of Limit of Detection (LOD), Limit of Quantitation (LOQ), Repeatability, the precision of intra-day and inter-day was carried out using standard mixtures. The recovery of the analyte was calculated as [A (mixture of sample and standard)-A(sample)]/A(standard) × 100%, in which A represents the relative peak area of analytes.Fig. 1Typical multiple reaction monitoring chromatograms of 5 standards and neurotransmitters side by side. Acetylcholine (ACH)(A);Dopamine(DA)(B);γ-Aminobutyric acid (GABA); (C) Glutamic acid (Glu); (D) and l-glutamine (GLN)(E).Fig 1 The results demonstrated that the LOD and LOQ of all five analytes were in the range of 0.26–3.77 and 0.88–12.58 ng/mL, which indicates that the present protocol is highly sensitive for ACH, GABA, GLU, and GLN, while the relative higher concentration (LOD 3.77 ng/ml, LOQ 12.58 ng/ml) in the sample is required for the detection of DA (Table 2). The variation (shown as Relative Standard Deviation (RSD)) of repeatability, intra-day precision and inter-day precision of all analytes should be lower than 15% [16] . In our experiments, all these parameters were lower than 5%. The optimal recovery should be between 80-120%. In our protocol, the recovery assay was determined at 3 (low to high) standard concentrations (5–100 ng/ml) (Table 3).
